reviewScope: Independent technical pre-incorporation review of the unsigned R4-corrected round-two remediation candidate. The review reproduced the bundled full and fixtures-only validators, independently checked all manifest hashes and exact canonical Git bytes, tested coherent authorization counterexamples, and perturbed validator expectations and declared-ID coverage in an isolated temporary copy. A confirmed authorization blocker is sufficient for SEND_BACK; this record does not claim that every possible new adversarial case has been exhausted.

integrityChecks.validatorReported: PASS R4 corrected candidate oracles only; next state is fresh-context preflight, not canonicalization

decision.rationale: All 45 manifest entries match and both validator modes pass. The R4 exact-path and missing/unlisted migration-action counterexamples are corrected, and the former declared-row execution gap is materially corrected. However, the shared protected-action decision still accepts coherently signed requests that violate the same manifest's provider resource, principal delegation, credential-lifetime, and upstream authority-scope constraints. A request for an unlisted repository returns ALLOW with installation-token and provider-request effects; the positive fixtures use 86400-second credentials despite 300/900/1800-second manifest limits; disallowed delegation edges are accepted; and authority item, Exam revision, product, and pod substitutions are silently ignored when absent downstream. Zero technical blocker/major is not met.

newFindings.title: Protected-action oracle still ignores enumerated resource, credential, delegation, and upstream authority scope

counterexamples.construction: Inspect and execute the unchanged positive fixtures for github.exam.candidate.commit, github.decision.record.commit, github.spend-authorization.commit, and migration.expand.
counterexamples.expected: DENY over-lifetime credentials according to each principal's exhaustive maxLifetimeSeconds.

Exam downstream/upstream limits are 900/900 seconds; decision limits 900/28800; spend limits 900/1800; migration limits 300/1800. readEnvelope checks only issuedAt <= now < expiresAt and never enforces the declared maximum or idle policy.

counterexamples.construction: Execute the unchanged positive decision, spend, and migration fixtures. Their signed delegation issuers are verified-human, org-budget-owner, and migration-authorizer, respectively, with recipients github-app-installation or schema-migration-runner.
counterexamples.expected: DENY an edge absent from the issuer principal's mayDelegateTo list, or revise the manifest to enumerate the intended narrowly scoped carrier delegation explicitly.
counterexamples.observed: All return ALLOW although each issuer's mayDelegateTo is an empty array. The decision verifies envelope coherence but never the manifest delegation edge.

counterexamples.construction: Start from valid fixtures, mutate and reseal authorityRecordBytes, then reseal upstreamBytes with the new authority record digest. For Exam set authority selectors item='attacker-item' and examRevision='attacker-revision'; for decision set item='attacker-item'; for spend set product='attacker-product' and pod='attacker-pod'. Leave the downstream request and every current authoritative CAS/replay/reservation snapshot unchanged.
counterexamples.expected: DENY incoherent item, Exam revision, product, or pod authority before any operational effect.
counterexamples.observed: All three requests return ALLOW with credentialAccess=1, installationToken=1, providerRequest=1. The comparison at line 267 explicitly skips any upstream selector whose downstream expected value is undefined. These required upstream scope fields are absent from the downstream selector set, so independent authority can concern a different scope.

newFindings.impact: The candidate claims an exhaustive deny-before-effect authorization oracle, yet cryptographic coherence alone can authorize an unlisted provider resource, overlong credential, forbidden delegation edge, or independently authorized record for another scope. This is not a publication-state dependency or a missing live implementation test: the candidate's own deterministic decision function returns an unsafe ALLOW for supplied bytes.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Enforce the selected action and upstream action's complete manifest contract, including resource selector mappings, principal lifetime/idle/one-use constraints and allowed delegation edges. Make every security-relevant upstream authority selector either present and byte-bound in the immutable downstream request or explicitly derived from a separately authenticated current authority context; never skip equality because a field is absent. Add schema and semantic checks for authority-record selector types and exact item/revision/product/pod linkage. Correct positive fixtures to satisfy the declared limits and delegation policy. Add coherent negative rows for wrong repository/resource, overlong/idle credentials, forbidden delegation edges, and each missing or substituted upstream scope field, requiring typed zero effects. Refresh all hashes and repeat a fresh independent pre-incorporation review.
